title: Students and police clash during Montreal protest over living costs

tea.why: Rising education, food, and housing costs affecting student financial security.
tea.want: Reform the student financial assistance program and increase funding for CEGEPs and universities.
tea.changed: Nov 13: Montreal police used tear gas and flash-bangs after rocks and projectiles were thrown.

summary: Thousands of students gathered in downtown Montreal for a demonstration called by the Coalition de résistance pour l'unité étudiante syndicale (CRUES) to protest rising education, food, and housing costs. The march started near Square Victoria and turned chaotic as clashes erupted with police officers in riot gear near Viger and St-Alexandre streets. According to police, protesters hurled rocks and projectiles at officers, leading authorities to deploy tear gas and flash-bang devices to disperse the crowds. Windows were broken around Square Victoria and Old Montreal. Quebec Higher Education Minister Elsie Lefebvre condemned the acts of violence and vandalism while acknowledging the right to protest. Police reported three arrests, including two for armed assault on a police officer and one for assault on a police officer, along with several incidents of property mischief.
organizers: Coalition de résistance pour l'unité étudiante syndicale (CRUES)
demands: Reform the student financial assistance program
Increase funding for CEGEPs and universities
Address rising education, food, and housing costs
response: According to CBC News and the Montreal Gazette, Montreal police deployed tear gas and flash-bang devices after projectiles were thrown. Quebec Higher Education Minister Elsie Lefebvre condemned acts of violence and vandalism while noting the government recognizes the right to protest.

updates.text: A student demonstration began around 2 p.m. near Square Victoria, bringing thousands into downtown Montreal.
Clashes broke out near Viger and St-Alexandre streets after projectiles were allegedly thrown at officers in riot gear.
Montreal police deployed tear gas and flash-bangs and reported three arrests for assaults on officers.
